questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I like how Bath, was not too far from Denmark as I wished the opportunity to be visited by my family and close friends. Also I have always liked the UK so I seemed like a fairly easy choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They were very good at helping after arrival and was very friendly when helping with anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a meeting with someone from the university where they made sure we were registered at the university and that we had registered for the right courses we wanted.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I missed the deadline for applying for accommodation and they were very sweet to inform me and helped me find a accommodation so for me it was pretty easy as they did the work for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is better, however I have not tried the experience of staying on campus. But I think you are more prone to go and explore the city when you are living in the city since campus is quite far form the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accommodation was in very bad shape

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to log into the website with you university login and had to fill in some information about yourself like who your emergency contact would be and what you're parents are doing for work. So all kinds of questions and then afterwards when you were able to log into the university email and "Samis" you were officially registered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the university with questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up swapping a course because it did not find it interesting, but otherwise I did the registration correctly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would say don't be afraid to email the university if you have any questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the research project did take a bit too much of my time however I found it very exciting so I can't really complain

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was around the same as back home, but if you take a BA course you have to get 40% in the exam to pass and the MA it is 50%

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SL52118 - Pharmacy research project
SL52135 - Synthesis of medicinal compounds
SL40105 - Global health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the SL52135 - Synthesis of medicinal compounds, but it is very chemistry heavy which I find very fun, but maybe not everyone would like it. Also the research project is good but that was mandatory.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I would say the prices were quite close to back home, but I was shocked that the accommodation was so expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: it is one of the biggest sports universities in England, so you can basically do any sport, and they have a lot of society's you can join to meet new people that have the same interests as yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To do some traveling around England because it is very fun to go around with people you meet.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around and see the nightlife because it is very lively. If you like hiking you can easily take the train to very nice hiking routes and come back same day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I met a lot of very sweet people so it felt very natural.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found that they actually are interested in speaking to you so don't be scared to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked the culture around rugby and enjoyed watching the games, however it was very expensive

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't be scared to meet new people and even if the people you meet at first are not you're type of people you are sure to meet someone else. Also try your best to just meet everyone in the start. Don't stay in your room and bedrot you need to go out and do stuff.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the people you are studying with if anything exciting is happening it can sometimes be hard to find the university planned events in my opinion. But they can be fun to attend, if you like things like gala.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people, it was such a giving experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taming the nerves of how its gonna go.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
